question: For each failure mode in the agent-failure taxonomy the user supplied, what control can tezgah enforce, at which enforcement point, and with what evidence?

evaluation.metric: share of taxonomy failure modes that have a mechanical control at a named enforcement point, measured against the installed rules on this checkout
evaluation.baseline: today's installed rules on branch research/agent-failure-controls: the PreToolUse gate refuses 7/19 pre-registered write-path cases and none of the 12 trajectory/consent cases (E1); the Stop rule refuses 8/10 explicit completion claims and 0/10 implicit ones (E2)

hypotheses.statement: The mechanical gate covers the write-time failure modes it was built for and covers none of the trajectory-time modes (repeat, order, partial failure, race, consent, secret, unvetted dependency).
The Stop rule detects explicit completion claims in both languages and misses the same claim stated as a state description.
Every failure mode in the taxonomy maps onto one of four enforcement points (prompt clause, tool gate, Stop gate, workspace check), and the modes with no enforcement point form the design backlog.
hypotheses.evidence: to_human/sections/A-..G-.md: every one of the 44 modes and 10 controls carries a Where line naming one of the four enforcement points

hypotheses.statement: The backlog modes have published mechanisms that can be implemented inside tezgah's existing hook surfaces without new dependencies or new hosts.
hypotheses.evidence: to_human/sections/: 41 fetched sources are cited by mechanism inside the design blocks; the two OpenAlex reviews were not fetched and are named as absent

hypotheses.statement: The ten priority controls in the user's checklist are mostly absent today: the evidence ledger implements the success-language gate, and the rest are prose or nothing.
hypotheses.evidence: to_human/sections/G-priority-controls.md: 1 implemented, 6 partial, 3 absent, verified against the cited file in the independent pass

hypotheses.statement: Every context block tezgah injects is static or capped, so the unbounded context in a session comes from the host's history, tool output and MCP schemas rather than from tezgah's own injection.

An enforced control changes the outcome of the work only where the model's unprompted default violates it; on tasks the model solves anyway the arms cannot separate, so a null block is a statement about the task set.
hypotheses.evidence: experiments/E4-mechanical-off-effect/results.jsonl (e02, e03: 5/5 in every arm including bare)
